utility.notes: KIUC is a genuinely distinct entity from the Hawaiian Electric Industries family (which owns HECO/MECO/HELCO) — it is a member-owned, not-for-profit electric cooperative and the only one of its kind in Hawaii, confirmed via both KIUC's own site and the Hawaii PUC's own page listing it as a separate PUC-regulated electric utility. Its interconnection rules (Schedule Q, its own Tariff No. 2 'Distributed Generation Interconnection Policies and Procedures') are entirely separate from Hawaiian Electric's Smart DER framework and must not be assumed to follow the same terms.

value.name: Kauai Island Utility Cooperative (KIUC)
value.notes: Per KIUC's own 'Rooftop Solar' page: customers must submit an interconnection request application for engineering review before installing a system (required by Hawaii PUC rules). KIUC's own compensation mechanism for exported PV energy is governed by 'Tariff No. 1, Schedule Q Modified — Purchase from Qualified Facilities 100 kW or less,' distinct from HECO/MECO/HELCO's NEM/Smart DER programs. KIUC also curtails (temporarily limits) Schedule Q customer exports at times, per its own published Curtailment FAQ — a distinct, KIUC-specific operational reality not present in the Smart DER islands' documentation reviewed this session.

city.notes: Kauai County covers the entire island of Kaua'i (and Ni'ihau) under a single county government, not separate incorporated municipalities. This record represents the county-wide AHJ; per the mission's Hawaii-specific instruction, no separate sub-county city pages are created beneath it. 'Lihue' (the County seat and Building Division's own address) is used as the representative city identifier.

permit_authority.value: County of Kaua'i Department of Public Works, Building Division

required_documents.notes: The County's own solar-specific permitting document (Kauai County Chapter 12 Building Code's 'Solar Permits' provision, and a State Energy Office-hosted 'Residential Photovoltaic Systems' guide summarizing the County's process) were both blocked this session: the Chapter 12 PDF triggered a file-download dialog in the browser and returned HTTP 403 via WebFetch; the energy.hawaii.gov mirror returned a Cloudflare challenge via browser and HTTP 403 via WebFetch. other_conditions: KIUC uses two distinct interconnection application forms depending on system size: one for systems less than 10 kW, and a separate one for systems greater than 10 kW
Customers must submit and receive engineering review approval of an interconnection request application before installing a PV system, per Hawaii PUC rules

value.name: Renewable Energy Technologies Income Tax Credit (RETITC) — Solar Energy System
value.description: Statewide Hawaii state income tax credit for solar energy systems (HRS 235-12.5): 35% of actual installed cost, capped at $5,000 per system for single-family residential property (lower of the two), $350 per unit for multi-family residential, or $500,000 per system for commercial property. A separate, higher-value $2,250 cap applies if the system's primary purpose is solar water heating rather than PV. Any utility rebate received must be deducted from system cost before computing the credit. Applies statewide to any Hawaii taxpayer regardless of county/island — a genuine reusable statewide fact, not utility- or county-specific.
value.eligibility: Any individual or corporate Hawaii state income taxpayer installing and placing in service an eligible solar energy system in the State; claimed on Form N-342. A taxpayer may elect a reduced (30% haircut) refundable version, or full refundability if income-qualified (AGI ≤$20,000 single / ≤$40,000 joint) or exempt.

rebates.notes: Verified directly from the Hawaii State Legislature's own hosted statute text (HRS 235-12.5). A 2026 legislative change (Act 24, Session Laws of Hawaii 2026) further modified the credit — the Department of Taxation issued Tax Information Release 2026-02 on this — but tax.hawaii.gov itself could not be loaded this session (persistent block), so the exact nature of the Act 24 change is not detailed here; the base statutory credit percentages/caps above come directly from the current codified statute text, not from the news commentary describing Act 24.
